title: Free and strict off-diagonal boundary comparison
statement: Let R be a normalized free-resolution datum from [lem-sf-cyclic-free-resolution-coordinates] and e1 the degree-minus-one additive Hom coordinates of [lem-sf-cyclic-free-hom-coordinates]. For every M,N and u in V^-1, the uniquely presented off-diagonal boundary of [lem-sf-cyclic-derived-off-diagonal-presentation] equals R.delta_M followed by e1 inverse of u. This identifies two specific morphisms, without assuming any additivity, naturality or exactness conclusion about the off-diagonal boundary.

source.place: Tags 0149, 0152 and 015F; parent calculus steps 1--2 and normalized free-resolution steps 5--9.

proof.text: For a strict presentation, construct the termwise free adjuncts of its splitting s and off-diagonal entry u0. R.summand and R.theta_eq, together with the recursion for Free.hom at -1, show on summand zero that R.d followed by the adjunct of s equals the adjunct of u0 followed by the inclusion. The splitting identity gives the counit square. Free.hom_ext extends the two equalities to morphisms of complexes.

Use these two squares and the identity of the quotient to form a morphism from the R free short exact sequence to the presented short exact sequence. Apply triangleOfSESδ_naturality. The localization counit formula and the exact-functor factorization identify the localized adjunct of u0 with the free adjunct of its underlying derived class. R.delta_fac then identifies the presented boundary with the corresponding R.delta pairing.

Obtain a strict presentation of cyclicDerivedOffDiagonalBoundary F u from its characterization. Naturality of R.delta and of the free counit transports its endpoint isomorphisms. The forgetting shift comparison and the shift equivalence unit/counit cancel the opposite shifts. Expanding the inverse of cyclicDerivedFreeShiftedHomEquiv identifies the transported pairing with R.delta.app M followed by that inverse applied to u.

proof_origin.place: Stacks 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), 0149 and 015F; the comparison calculation already proved privately in CyclicDerivedOffDiagonalPresentation, adapted by B2 to the supplied normalized resolution R. The proof is fully written in Lean, with no split-off obligations.

lean.statement:
theorem cyclicDerivedFreeBoundary_comparison (R : CyclicDerivedFreeResolution F)
    {M N : DerivedCategory (IsoAlgebra F)} (u : CyclicDerivedHom F M N (-1)) :
    cyclicDerivedOffDiagonalBoundary F u =
      R.delta.app M ≫ (cyclicDerivedFreeShiftedHomEquiv F M N).symm u
